one_month_reasoning: No Nebius earnings in the window: Q2 was reported 2026-08-12 and the investor-events page lists nothing scheduled; Q3 results should come around mid-November by last year's calendar (judgment), so outside the window. What does fall in the window: (1) CME/NYMEX Silicon Data H100 and B200 rental-index futures, targeted for 2026-10-05 pending CFTC (src 18). That gives a public reference price for GPU rent, which helps if rents stay firm and hurts if the curve prices in decline; neutral to slightly positive given rental indices are still near highs (Ornn H100 $2.92, B200 $7.96 on Oct 1). (2) Hyperscaler Q3 earnings and capex guidance in the last week of October (MSFT/META/GOOGL/AMZN; dates are judgment). This is the biggest swing factor for neocloud sentiment, and capex has kept being revised up, so it leans mildly positive. (3) Possible 2027 guidance or deal news; mgmt said formal 2027 guidance comes 'later in 2026', most likely with Q3. (4) Overhang: Burry swapped his short for June-2027 puts with double-digit strikes, insiders have kept selling (Form 4s in Sep), holders of converts received ~15.8M exchanged shares, and the 10Y is at 5.24%. Net: no strong directional edge, so I centre on today's $232.28 with ~28% monthly lognormal sigma, a little below the 106%/sqrt(12) realized figure because no company event falls in the window.

fair_value.method: Blend of a capacity-driven DCF ($184 12-month forward; WACC 13.5%, g 3%, fleet yield $12.5-15M/MW fading to $12M, 55% terminal EBITDA margin, $25M/MW capex plus 6-year GPU refresh) at 45%, 8.5x 2028E EBITDA of $12.0B ($263) at 35%, and 4.9x NTM EV/sales ($272) at 20%, giving ~$229, about today's price. The intrinsic DCF sits below the market-multiple methods because capital intensity and GPU repricing risk absorb most of the early cash flow.

methods.name: DCF

Sensitivity: WACC 12/13.5/15% -> $249/$184/$136; fleet yield +/-20% -> $318/$49.

bear.story: GPU rental pricing rolls over in 2027 as Vera Rubin supply and competitors' GW-scale capacity arrive, so new-deal yields fall back toward $10-12M/MW. A hyperscaler capex digestion or an 'AI bubble' scare (Polymarket gives 18% by mid-2027) shuts equity-linked funding, which forces dilution at low prices or slower builds. Execution slippage on >1GW/yr. DCF with fleet yield -20% gives ~$50-80; multiples compress to CoreWeave-like levels.

base.story: 0.8-1GW active in H1-27 pushes ARR to ~$13-16B by mid-2027 and 2027 revenue lands near consensus ($12-13B) with 45%+ margins. 2027 guidance is solid but already expected. Continued convert/ATM dilution and $25-30B of 2027 capex keep FCF deeply negative. The stock trades on 8-9x forward EBITDA, about where it is now.

bull.story: 2027 guidance 'shocks' (newsletter view: $16-20B ARR by mid-2027). Short-term deals at $40-50M/MW and auctions show scarcity pricing persisting into 2028, revenue tracks BNP's $14B/2027 and $31B/2028, and prepayments self-fund over half of capex. The market pays 10-12x 2028 EBITDA, in line with BNP's $399 target.

thesis_break_reason: Below ~$120 (about -48%, where the DCF lands with fleet yields 20% under base), the market would most likely be saying the scarcity-pricing thesis has failed rather than showing ordinary 100%-vol noise. That would look like: GPU rental indices (Ornn/Silicon Data/Mercatus) falling well below 2025 lows, new deals repricing below the 2026 $12M/MW base, a prepayment or capacity-delivery failure on Meta/Microsoft or the Q2 neolab contracts, or financing stress (convert/ABS markets closing) forcing a cut to the >1GW/yr build.

reasoning: Facts: Q2-26 revenue $582M (+454%), group adj. EBITDA margin 41% (AI cloud 50%), ARR $3.0B, 2026 guide ARR $7-9B / revenue $3.0-3.4B / capex $20-25B, Q2 deals at $20-25M/MW with 1y10m payback, 5GW contracted power by YE26, >1GW/yr deployment from 2027 (company letter, 6-K). Balance sheet: ~$13.5B debt after the $5B August converts, ~288M basic shares. Alternative-lane evidence: GPU rental indices confirm the scarcity pricing behind the bull case (H100 up ~70% from the Oct-25 low to $2.92 on Oct 1; B200 ~$8; H200 premium widened in July), but Mercatus shows H100 flat over 30 days, so pricing may be plateauing. Job postings reached an all-time high of 237/week in July and headcount roughly doubled (AltIndex, corroborated by Revelio), consistent with real build-out. Newsletter sentiment is very bullish (MVC 'never been more bullish', $16-20B mid-27 ARR framing; BNP via Exencial at $399, 2027/28 revenue 15-24% above consensus). Bearish signals: Burry moved from short stock to June-2027 puts, Polymarket gives 8% to an AI-bubble burst by YE26 and 18% by mid-2027 (the 2027 leg is thin, ~$9k volume), there is steady insider selling, and the 10Y is at 5.24%. Valuation: an explicit DCF on capacity x yield with full GPU refresh capex gives only $184 a year out at a 13.5% WACC and is extremely sensitive (+/-20% yield moves it to $318/$49). Market-multiple methods on consensus 2028 give $263-272. The blend of ~$229 is roughly today's price, so I have no strong directional view. Distribution: an equal blend of a three-scenario lognormal mixture (bear $100 / base $235 / bull $420 at 25/50/25%) and a single lognormal centred at $228 with 80% sigma (below the 106% realized, since forward vol on a $70B name should moderate). The result is P(>=232) ~0.50 with fat tails on both sides. Research limits: Reddit's JSON endpoint was blocked and X was not reachable, so social-forum sentiment comes only indirectly through newsletters and press. Twelve Data estimates and Alpha Vantage were unavailable (plan/rate limits), so consensus is inferred from BNP's stated premium to consensus.
